reference_title: Eurocode 7: Geotechnical design - Part 2: Ground investigation and testing
chapter_title: Field tests in soil and rock

sections.title: General
sections.summary: Field tests are linked to sampling by excavation and drilling to give stratification and parameters or direct design input; they are planned for geology, structure, parameters needed and design method, chosen from the EN ISO 22476 tests of this Section (CPT, PMT and dilatometer, SPT, DP, WST, FVT, DMT, PLT); Table 2.1 gives their applicability; geophysics may supplement.
sections.body: (1)P Field tests shall be linked to sampling by excavation and drilling so as to give the ground stratification and geotechnical parameters or direct input to design methods (see EN 1997-1:2004, 3.3). (2)P Field tests shall be planned for the geology and stratification, the type of structure, possible foundation and expected construction work, the parameters needed, and the design method (see also Section 2). (3) Tests or combinations should be chosen from the EN ISO 22476 types covered here: cone penetration, pressuremeter and dilatometer, standard penetration, dynamic probing, weight sounding, field vane, flat dilatometer and plate loading tests; Table 2.1 gives a broad overview of their applicability by ground. (4) Other complementary internationally recognised methods, e.g. geophysics, may be used. (p. 40)
key_points: Link field tests to sampling by excavation and drilling (p. 40).
Plan tests for geology, structure, parameters needed and design method (p. 40).
Choose among CPT, PMT/dilatometer, SPT, DP, WST, FVT, DMT and PLT (p. 40).
Table 2.1 gives a broad overview of test applicability (p. 40).
sections.applicability: Frames the planning requirements common to every field test type covered in the remainder of Section 4.

sections.title: General requirements
sections.summary: Heading for the general requirements of field tests: planning a test programme (4.2.1), execution (4.2.2) and evaluation (4.2.3).
sections.body: Heading for 4.2.1 to 4.2.3; it has no text of its own. (p. 40)

sections.title: Planning a specific test programme
sections.summary: Besides 2.3, 2.4 and 4.1 (2), the programme establishes the expected ground profile, total depth, ground surface elevation and groundwater level, and chooses tests and equipment for the best technical and economic result (see Table 2.1 and B.2).
sections.body: (1)P Beyond the recommendations of 2.3 and the requirements of 2.4 and 4.1 (2), the expected ground profile, the desired total depth of investigation, and the ground surface elevation and, if applicable, groundwater level shall be established. (2)P The choice of field tests and equipment shall aim at the best technical and economic solution for the purpose. NOTE: see also Table 2.1 and B.2. (p. 40)
key_points: Establish expected profile, total depth, surface elevation and groundwater level (p. 40).
Choose tests and equipment for the best technical and economic solution (p. 40).
sections.applicability: Cross-cutting planning, execution, and evaluation requirements that apply to every field test type in Section 4.

sections.title: Execution
sections.summary: Equipment and procedures follow EN ISO 22476-1 to -9, -12 and -13 (WST and DMT in CEN ISO/TS 22476-10 and -11); results that contradict the initial information prompt extra tests or other methods, and the client is told at once if the depth is not reached.
sections.body: (1)P Equipment and procedures for the tests of this Section shall meet EN ISO 22476-1 to EN ISO 22476-9, EN ISO 22476-12 and EN ISO 22476-13. NOTE: the weight sounding test and the flat dilatometer test are covered by CEN ISO/TS 22476-10 and CEN ISO/TS 22476-11 respectively. (2)P If ongoing results do not match the initial information on the site or aim (Section 2), additional measures such as more tests or a change of test method shall be considered. (3) The client should be told immediately if the desired depth is not reached. (p. 41)
key_points: Equipment and procedures per EN ISO 22476-1 to -9, -12 and -13 (p. 41).
Unexpected results prompt more tests or other methods (p. 41).
Tell the client at once if the investigation depth is not reached (p. 41).
sections.applicability: Cross-cutting planning, execution, and evaluation requirements that apply to every field test type in Section 4.

sections.title: Evaluation
sections.summary: Evaluation uses all ground information and the Section 3 sampling results, considers ground and equipment influences and anisotropy, checks each correlation's suitability for the project, and for Annexes D to K confirms the site matches the correlation's boundary conditions, with local experience where available.
sections.body: (1)P Any additional ground information shall be considered in evaluating field tests, especially when deriving parameters or coefficients. (2)P Results of sampling by drilling and excavation (Section 3) shall be available and used. (3)P Ground and equipment influences on the measured parameters shall be considered; with anisotropic soil or rock, attention shall be paid to the loading axis relative to the anisotropy. (4)P The suitability of any correlation shall be considered for each project. (5)P With Annexes D to K, the site conditions (soil type, uniformity coefficient, consistency index etc.) shall be compatible with the correlation's boundary conditions, confirmed by local experience if available. NOTE 1: Annexes D to K give example correlations for derived values and for applying test values to design. NOTE 2: X.3 lists examples of correlations for derived values and of direct design use of test results (p. 41). (pp. 41 to 42)
key_points: Use the Section 3 sampling results in evaluating field tests (p. 41).
Mind the loading axis relative to anisotropy (p. 41).
Check each correlation's suitability for the project (p. 41).
Annexes D to K: site must match the correlation's boundary conditions (p. 41).
sections.applicability: Cross-cutting planning, execution, and evaluation requirements that apply to every field test type in Section 4.

sections.title: Cone penetration and piezocone penetration tests (CPT, CPTU, CPTM)
sections.summary: Heading for cone and piezocone penetration tests (CPT, CPTU, CPTM): objectives (4.3.1), requirements (4.3.2), evaluation (4.3.3) and use of results (4.3.4).
sections.body: Heading for 4.3.1 to 4.3.4; it has no text of its own. (p. 42)
sections.applicability: CPT/CPTU/CPTM test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex D derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Objectives
sections.summary: The CPT pushes a cone (and friction sleeve) at constant rate to measure cone resistance qc and sleeve friction; CPTU adds pore pressure at the cone base. Results serve mainly for soil profiles with sampling, and also for strength and deformation parameters, direct design, pile length and resistance, and shallow foundation size.
sections.body: (1) The CPT determines the resistance of soil and soft rock to penetration of a cone and the local friction on a sleeve. (2)P A cone penetrometer is pushed vertically at a constant rate on push rods; it comprises the cone and, if appropriate, a cylindrical shaft or friction sleeve; the cone resistance (qc) and, if appropriate, sleeve friction shall be measured. (3)P In electrical CPTs all readings shall come from sensors in the penetrometer. (4) Mechanical CPTs generally measure remotely. (5) The CPTU is an electrical CPT that also measures pore pressure during penetration at the level of the cone base. (6) CPTU results should be used mainly to determine a soil profile with sampling results (Section 3) or in comparison with other field tests. (7) They may also give strength and deformation parameters of soil and soft rock where penetration is possible, and direct design input, generally in coarse and fine soil and possibly other deposits. (8) They may also give pile length and compressive or tensile resistance, or the dimensions of shallow foundations. (p. 42)
key_points: CPT measures cone resistance qc and sleeve friction at constant penetration rate (p. 42).
CPTU adds pore water pressure at the level of the cone base (p. 42).
Use mainly for soil profiles together with sampling (p. 42).
Also for strength, deformation, pile length and resistance, shallow foundation size (p. 42).
sections.applicability: CPT/CPTU/CPTM test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex D derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Specific requirements
sections.summary: Tests follow EN ISO 22476-1 (electrical CPT, CPTU) or EN ISO 22476-12 (CPTM); the programme fixes the test type and the depth and duration of any dissipation tests; deviations are justified and their influence reported.
sections.body: (1)P Tests shall be performed and reported by a method meeting EN ISO 22476-1 for the electrical CPT and CPTU or EN ISO 22476-12 for the CPTM. (2)P Beyond 4.2.1, the programme shall decide the type of cone test and the depth and duration of pore pressure dissipation tests if applicable. (3)P Deviations from those standards shall be justified and reported, with comment on their influence on results. (p. 42)
key_points: CPT and CPTU per EN ISO 22476-1; CPTM per EN ISO 22476-12 (p. 42).
Decide test type and dissipation test depths and durations (p. 42).
sections.applicability: CPT/CPTU/CPTM test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex D derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Evaluation of test results
sections.summary: Evaluation uses the EN ISO 22476-1 or -12 field and test reports and considers ground influences on penetration resistance; in clays the cone resistance corrected for pore pressure, qt, should be used.
sections.body: (1)P Beyond 4.2, the field and test reports per EN ISO 22476-1 or EN ISO 22476-12 shall be used for evaluation. (2)P Possible ground influences on penetration resistance shall be considered; e.g. in clays the cone resistance corrected for pore water pressure effects (qt) should be used. (p. 43)
key_points: In clays, use qt, the cone resistance corrected for pore water pressure (p. 43).
sections.applicability: CPT/CPTU/CPTM test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex D derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Use of test results and derived values
sections.summary: Heading for the use of CPT results and derived values: spread foundation bearing resistance and settlement (4.3.4.1) and pile bearing resistance (4.3.4.2).
sections.body: Heading for 4.3.4.1 and 4.3.4.2; it has no text of its own. (p. 43)
sections.applicability: CPT/CPTU/CPTM test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex D derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Bearing resistance and settlement of spread foundations
sections.summary: Spread foundations from CPT use semi-empirical or analytical methods. cu = (qc - σv0)/Nk (Eq. 4.1) or (qt - σv0)/Nkt (Eq. 4.2); φ' from qc by local experience (D.1, D.2); E' from qc by local experience (D.1); semi-empirical settlement in coarse soil (D.3); Eoed = α × qc (Eq. 4.3, D.4) or a stress-dependent Eoed (D.5).
sections.body: (1)P Bearing resistance or settlement of a spread foundation from CPT results shall use a semi-empirical or analytical method (e.g. EN 1997-1:2004, Annex D or F). (2)P A semi-empirical method shall be applied with all its features; e.g. the semi-empirical settlement method from CPT (D.3) uses only Young's modulus derived from qc. (3) With the sample analytical bearing method of EN 1997-1:2004, Annex D, the undrained shear strength of fine soil may come from Eq. 4.1 for a CPT or Eq. 4.2 for a CPTU. (4) With that method, φ' may be taken from qc on local experience, allowing for depth effects; NOTE 1: D.1 gives ranges for quartz and feldspar sands where depth effects need not be considered; NOTE 2: D.2 gives a φ'-qc correlation for poorly graded sands, to be taken as conservative. (5) More elaborate methods may derive φ' from qc with effective vertical stress, compressibility and over-consolidation ratio (p. 43). (6) In an adjusted elasticity settlement method (EN 1997-1:2004, Annex F), the qc to drained Young's modulus (E') correlation depends on whether the method is semi-empirical or theoretical. (7) Semi-empirical settlement methods may be used in coarse soil (example in D.3). (8) In a theoretical elastic method, E' may come from qc on local experience (D.1 gives values for quartz and feldspar sands). (9) Eoed and qc correlations may be used for settlement, often Eq. 4.3 with α from local experience (example in D.4). (10) A stress-dependent Eoed based on qc may be used in theoretical elastic methods (EN 1997-1:2004, Annex F); D.5 gives correlations to be taken as conservative (p. 44). (pp. 43 to 44)
key_points: Use a semi-empirical or analytical method, applying all features of a semi-empirical one (p. 43).
cu from CPT by Eq. 4.1 or from CPTU by Eq. 4.2; Nk, Nkt from local experience (p. 43).
φ' from qc on local experience; D.1 ranges, D.2 conservative correlation (p. 43).
E' from qc on local experience; D.1 gives sand values (p. 44).
Eoed = α × qc (Eq. 4.3), α from local experience; D.4 and D.5 examples (p. 44).

equations.description: cu = (qc - σv0) / Nk; undrained shear strength of fine soil from a CPT, qc cone penetration resistance, σv0 initial total vertical overburden stress at the depth considered, Nk coefficient from local experience or reliable correlations (p. 43)
cu = (qt - σv0) / Nkt; from a CPTU, qt cone resistance corrected for pore water pressure effects, Nkt coefficient from local experience or reliable correlations (p. 43)
Eoed = α × qc; oedometer modulus from cone resistance, α correlation factor depending on local experience (p. 44)

sections.applicability: CPT/CPTU/CPTM test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex D derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Pile bearing resistance
sections.summary: Ultimate compressive or tensile pile resistance (EN 1997-1:2004, 7.6.2.3 or 7.6.3.3) from CPT results uses calculation rules from locally established correlations between static load tests and CPT; D.6 and D.7 give examples.
sections.body: (1)P If the ultimate compressive or tensile pile resistance (EN 1997-1:2004, 7.6.2.3 or 7.6.3.3) is derived from CPT results, calculation rules based on locally established correlations between static load test and CPT results shall be used. NOTE 1: D.6 gives such correlations for coarse soil. NOTE 2: D.7 gives an example of the compressive resistance of a single pile from qc values. (p. 44)
key_points: Pile resistance from CPT needs locally established load test correlations (p. 44).
D.6 and D.7 give examples (p. 44).
sections.applicability: CPT/CPTU/CPTM test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex D derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Pressuremeter tests (PMT)
sections.summary: Heading for pressuremeter tests (PMT): objectives (4.4.1), requirements (4.4.2), evaluation (4.4.3) and use of results (4.4.4).
sections.body: Heading for 4.4.1 to 4.4.4; it has no text of its own. (p. 45)
sections.applicability: PMT/dilatometer test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex E Menard-pressuremeter derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Objectives
sections.summary: The PMT measures in-situ deformation of soil and soft rock by expanding a cylindrical flexible membrane under pressure in a pre-formed, self-bored or pushed hole, recording pressure and expansion; it gives strength and deformation or pressuremeter parameters and stress-strain curves in fine soil and soft rock.
sections.body: (1) The pressuremeter test measures in situ the deformation of soil and soft rock caused by expanding a cylindrical flexible membrane under pressure. (2)P A probe with the membrane is inserted into a pre-formed borehole, by self-boring or by full-displacement pushing; at the chosen depth it is expanded and pressure and expansion are recorded up to the device's maximum expansion. NOTE: expansion is measured from radial displacement or calculated from the membrane's volume change. (3) The test should be used to derive strength and/or deformation parameters or specific pressuremeter parameters. (4) Results may give stress-strain curves in fine soil and soft rock. (p. 45)
key_points: PMT expands a cylindrical membrane and records pressure and expansion (p. 45).
Gives strength, deformation or pressuremeter parameters (p. 45).
Stress-strain curves in fine soil and soft rock (p. 45).
sections.applicability: PMT/dilatometer test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex E Menard-pressuremeter derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Specific requirements
sections.summary: The pressuremeter type is specified: pre-bored PBP (e.g. FDT, EN ISO 22476-5), Ménard MPM (EN ISO 22476-4), self-boring SBP (-6) or full-displacement FDP (-8). One procedure gives the Ménard modulus EM and limit pressure pLM; another other stiffness and strength parameters; deviations are justified.
sections.body: (1)P The pressuremeter type shall be specified in the programme. (2)P Four apparatus types are generally available, each with its standard: pre-bored pressuremeters (PBP), e.g. the flexible dilatometer test (FDT), per EN ISO 22476-5; the Ménard pressuremeter (MPM), a specific form of PBP, per EN ISO 22476-4; the self-boring pressuremeter (SBP) per EN ISO 22476-6; and the full-displacement pressuremeter (FDP) per EN ISO 22476-8. NOTE: PBP and MPM go into a hole made for the test; the SBP bores itself in with a cutting head so the probe replaces the removed material; the FDP is usually pushed in behind an integral cone; the MPM may sometimes be pushed or driven; probes take various forms by installation and measuring system. (3) Two basic procedures may be used: one for a pressuremeter modulus (EM) and limit pressure (pLM) for Ménard-based design procedures, and one for other stiffness and strength parameters (p. 45). (4)P Tests shall be performed and reported by a method meeting the standard of the instrument used (4.4.2 (2)P). (5)P Deviations shall be justified with comment on their influence (p. 46). (pp. 45 to 46)
key_points: Specify the pressuremeter type: PBP, MPM, SBP or FDP (p. 45).
PBP/FDT EN ISO 22476-5; MPM -4; SBP -6; FDP -8 (p. 45).
One procedure gives EM and pLM for Ménard-based design (p. 45).
sections.applicability: PMT/dilatometer test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex E Menard-pressuremeter derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Evaluation of test results
sections.summary: Pressure is corrected for membrane stiffness; radial displacement becomes cavity strain (corrected for membrane compression and thinning in weak rock); volume readings are corrected for system expansion. Evaluation uses the EN ISO 22476-4, -5, -6 or -8 reports, and Table 4.1 lists additional plots.
sections.body: (1)P If necessary, applied pressure shall be corrected for membrane stiffness to get the true pressure on the cavity wall. (2)P With a radial displacement pressuremeter, displacements shall be converted to cavity strain and, in weak rock, corrected for membrane compression and thinning. (3)P With a volume displacement type (e.g. MPM), volume readings shall be corrected for system expansion. (4)P Beyond 4.2, the field and test reports per EN ISO 22476-4, -5, -6 or -8 for the test type shall be the basis of further evaluation. (5) Besides the plots each equipment standard requires, the additional plots of Table 4.1 should be considered (p. 46). (p. 46)
key_points: Correct pressure for membrane stiffness (p. 46).
Convert radial displacement to cavity strain (p. 46).
Correct MPM volume readings for system expansion (p. 46).
Consider the additional plots of Table 4.1 (p. 46).
tables: Table 4.1: A list of additional plots - probe; ground type; abscissa; ordinate, as printed. Radial displacement type: self-bored, pushed in; all; cavity strain for each arm; applied pressure. Pre-bored; all; cavity strain for each pair of arms; applied pressure. Self bored; all; initial cavity strain for each arm; applied pressure. All; all; cavity strain for unload-reload cycle for each arm; applied pressure. All; clay; logarithm of cavity strain for each arm; applied pressure. All; sands; natural logarithm of current cavity strain for each arm; natural logarithm of effective applied pressure. Volume displacement type (except MPM) (a): pre-bored; all; volume change; applied pressure. Pre-bored; all; rate of change of volume; applied pressure. (a) For MPM tests the pressure is plotted as abscissa and the volume change as ordinate
sections.applicability: PMT/dilatometer test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex E Menard-pressuremeter derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Use of test results and derived values
sections.summary: Heading for the use of PMT results and derived values: general criteria (4.4.4.1), bearing resistance (4.4.4.2) and settlement (4.4.4.3) of spread foundations, and pile bearing resistance (4.4.4.4).
sections.body: Heading for 4.4.4.1 to 4.4.4.4; it has no text of its own. (p. 47)
sections.applicability: PMT/dilatometer test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex E Menard-pressuremeter derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: General criteria
sections.summary: Indirect or analytical design derives shear strength and shear modulus from the pressuremeter curve by methods for the test and equipment; a direct or semi-empirical method is applied with all its features, e.g. MPM settlement uses only the Ménard modulus EM (E.2).
sections.body: (1)P For an indirect or analytical method, shear strength and shear modulus shall be derived from the pressuremeter curve by methods for the test and equipment type. (2)P A direct or semi-empirical method shall be applied with all its features. NOTE: direct foundation procedures use field test measurements directly instead of conventional soil properties. (3)P E.g. the semi-empirical MPM settlement method shall use only the modulus EM from Ménard tests. NOTE: settlement examples are in E.2. (p. 47)
key_points: Derive shear strength and shear modulus from the pressuremeter curve (p. 47).
Semi-empirical MPM settlement uses only the Ménard modulus EM (p. 47).
sections.applicability: PMT/dilatometer test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex E Menard-pressuremeter derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Bearing resistance of spread foundations
sections.summary: A semi-empirical bearing method is followed in full, including the pressuremeter type it was built on, with EN ISO 22476-4 (Ménard method in EN 1997-1:2004, Annex E; example E.1); analytical methods need local experience; φ' from SBP in coarse soil by theory, from FDP and PBP by empirical correlations.
sections.body: (1)P A semi-empirical method shall be followed in all aspects, especially the pressuremeter type used to establish it, and EN ISO 22476-4 shall be followed. NOTE 1: the Ménard semi-empirical method is in EN 1997-1:2004, Annex E. NOTE 2: E.1 gives an example bearing resistance calculation. (2) With an analytical method, soil strength may be found by empirical and theoretical methods only on local experience (examples in EN 1997-1:2004, Annex D). (3) φ' may be found from an SBP test in coarse soil by theory, and from FDP and PBP tests by empirical correlations, only on local experience. (p. 47)
key_points: Follow a semi-empirical method in all aspects, incl. pressuremeter type (p. 47).
Ménard method in EN 1997-1:2004, Annex E; example in E.1 (p. 47).
φ' from SBP by theory or FDP/PBP correlations, on local experience only (p. 47).
sections.applicability: PMT/dilatometer test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex E Menard-pressuremeter derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Settlement of spread foundations
sections.summary: Spread foundation settlement may come from MPM tests by a semi-empirical method (example E.2); analytical methods interpret stiffness by theoretical models only on local experience (EN 1997-1:2004, Annex F).
sections.body: (1) Settlement of spread foundations may be found from MPM tests by a semi-empirical method (example in E.2). (2) With an analytical method, soil stiffness may be found by theoretical interpretation models only on local experience (examples in EN 1997-1:2004, Annex F). (p. 47)
key_points: MPM settlement by a semi-empirical method; example in E.2 (p. 47).
Analytical stiffness interpretation only on local experience (p. 47).
sections.applicability: PMT/dilatometer test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex E Menard-pressuremeter derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Pile bearing resistance
sections.summary: Ultimate compressive pile resistance may come directly from stress-controlled tests (example E.3); indirect derivation of base and shaft resistance by analytical methods needs local experience.
sections.body: (1) Ultimate compressive resistance of piles may be derived directly from stress-controlled tests (example in E.3). (2) If compressive or tensile resistance is derived indirectly, an analytical method may give base and shaft resistance only on local experience. (p. 48)
key_points: Pile compressive resistance directly from stress-controlled tests; example E.3 (p. 48).
Indirect base and shaft resistance only on local experience (p. 48).
sections.applicability: PMT/dilatometer test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex E Menard-pressuremeter derived-value correlations for bearing resistance, settlement, and pile capacity.

sections.title: Flexible dilatometer test (FDT)
sections.summary: Heading for the flexible dilatometer test (FDT): objectives (4.5.1), requirements (4.5.2), evaluation (4.5.3) and use of results (4.5.4).
sections.body: Heading for 4.5.1 to 4.5.4; it has no text of its own. (p. 48)
sections.applicability: FDT (RDT/SDT) test procedure and use for deformation-based serviceability checks of foundations on soil or rock.

sections.title: Objectives
sections.summary: The FDT measures deformability of rock (RDT) and soil (SDT) from radial expansion of a borehole section under known uniform pressure from a cylindrical probe; RDT mainly in soft and hard rock, SDT in soft to stiff soil, giving deformability with depth, creep in intact rock, or index logging where core is poor.
sections.body: (1) The flexible dilatometer test measures in situ the deformability of rock (rock dilatometer test, RDT) and soil (soil dilatometer test, SDT) from the radial expansion of a borehole section under a known uniform radial pressure from a cylindrical probe. (2)P A probe with an expandable flexible membrane is placed in a borehole and the radial displacement is measured at chosen times or semi-continuously while it is inflated under known pressure. (3) The RDT should be used mainly in soft and hard rock and the SDT primarily in soft to stiff soil, for profiles of deformability with depth. (4) Results may give in-situ deformation and creep properties of intact rock. (5) In fragile or clayey rock and fractured or closely jointed ground with poor core recovery, the test may serve for rapid index logging and for comparing relative deformability of strata. (p. 48)
key_points: RDT for rock, SDT for soil: radial expansion under known uniform pressure (p. 48).
Gives deformability profiles; creep in intact rock (p. 48).
Index logging where core recovery is poor (p. 48).
sections.applicability: FDT (RDT/SDT) test procedure and use for deformation-based serviceability checks of foundations on soil or rock.

sections.title: Specific requirements
sections.summary: The device's specific requirements are specified; tests follow EN ISO 22476-5, and deviations are justified with their influence reported.
sections.body: (1)P The specific requirements of the device shall be specified in the programme. (2)P Tests shall be performed and reported per EN ISO 22476-5. (3)P Deviations shall be justified with comment on their influence. (p. 48)
key_points: Flexible dilatometer tests per EN ISO 22476-5 (p. 48).
sections.applicability: FDT (RDT/SDT) test procedure and use for deformation-based serviceability checks of foundations on soil or rock.

sections.title: Evaluation of test results
sections.summary: Evaluation uses the EN ISO 22476-5 field and test reports; interpretation needs the Poisson's ratio of the ground, known or assumed.
sections.body: (1)P Beyond 4.2, the EN ISO 22476-5 field and test reports for the test type shall be used (p. 48). (2) Interpretation requires the Poisson's ratio of the soil or rock to be known or assumed (p. 49). (pp. 48 to 49)
key_points: Interpretation needs a known or assumed Poisson's ratio (p. 49).
sections.applicability: FDT (RDT/SDT) test procedure and use for deformation-based serviceability checks of foundations on soil or rock.

sections.title: Use of test results and derived values
sections.summary: Dilatometer results may check spread foundation serviceability by deformation analysis, taking E equal to the dilatometer modulus EFDT for linearly elastic isotropic ground; analytical methods derive shear modulus from the dilatometer curve.
sections.body: (1) Dilatometer results may be used to check the serviceability limit state of spread foundations on soil or rock by deformation analysis. (2) Young's modulus (E) may then be taken equal to the dilatometer modulus (EFDT), assuming linearly elastic isotropic ground. (3)P For indirect or analytical methods, shear modulus shall be derived from the dilatometer curve by methods for that test type. (p. 49)
key_points: Check spread foundation serviceability by deformation analysis (p. 49).
E may be taken equal to EFDT for linearly elastic isotropic ground (p. 49).
sections.applicability: FDT (RDT/SDT) test procedure and use for deformation-based serviceability checks of foundations on soil or rock.

sections.title: Standard penetration test (SPT)
sections.summary: Heading for the standard penetration test (SPT): objectives (4.6.1), requirements (4.6.2), evaluation (4.6.3) and use of results (4.6.4).
sections.body: Heading for 4.6.1 to 4.6.4; it has no text of its own. (p. 49)
sections.applicability: SPT test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex F derived-value correlations for phi', settlement, and pile bearing resistance in sand.

sections.title: Objectives
sections.summary: The SPT measures resistance at the borehole base to dynamic penetration of a split barrel sampler (or solid cone) and gives disturbed samples: a 63,5 kg hammer falls 760 mm, and the blows N for 300 mm penetration after a seating drive are the resistance; mainly for coarse soil strength and deformation.
sections.body: (1) The SPT determines the resistance of soil at the base of a borehole to dynamic penetration of a split barrel sampler (or solid cone) and obtains disturbed samples for identification. (2)P The sampler shall be driven by a hammer of 63,5 kg mass dropped onto an anvil or drive head from 760 mm; the number of blows (N) for 300 mm of sampler penetration, after penetration under gravity and below a seating drive, is the penetration resistance. (3) The test should be used mainly for strength and deformation properties of coarse soil. (4) Valuable additional data may also come from other soils. (p. 49)
key_points: Hammer 63,5 kg falling 760 mm onto an anvil or drive head (p. 49).
N = blows for 300 mm penetration after the seating drive (p. 49).
Mainly for strength and deformation of coarse soil (p. 49).
sections.applicability: SPT test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex F derived-value correlations for phi', settlement, and pile bearing resistance in sand.

sections.title: Specific requirements
sections.summary: SPTs are performed and reported per EN ISO 22476-3; deviations are justified with their influence on results commented on.
sections.body: (1)P Tests shall be performed and reported per EN ISO 22476-3. (2)P Deviations shall be justified with comment on their influence on results. (p. 49)
key_points: SPT per EN ISO 22476-3 (p. 49).
sections.applicability: SPT test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex F derived-value correlations for phi', settlement, and pile bearing resistance in sand.

sections.title: Evaluation of test results
sections.summary: Evaluation uses the EN ISO 22476-3 reports; SPT design methods are empirical, so correction factors are considered; the energy ratio Er (measured to theoretical energy) must be known to correct N; in sands, rod length energy loss and overburden are allowed for, and liners or a solid cone corrected for.
sections.body: (1)P Beyond 4.2, the EN ISO 22476-3 field and test reports shall be used. (2)P SPT-based foundation design methods are empirical and operating methods have been adapted for reliability, so correction factors shall be considered (EN ISO 22476-3) (p. 49). (3)P The energy ratio (Er) of the equipment has to be known for quantitative foundation evaluation or comparing results: Er is the ratio of the actual energy Emeas (measured in calibration) delivered by the drive-weight assembly into the rod below the anvil to the theoretical energy (Etheor) of the assembly; N shall be corrected accordingly (EN ISO 22476-3). (4) In sands, rod-length energy losses and the effective overburden pressure should be allowed for (EN ISO 22476-3:2005, A.2 and A.4). (5) Other corrections should be considered, e.g. for liners (EN ISO 22476-3:2005, A.3) or a solid cone (p. 50). (pp. 49 to 50)
key_points: SPT design methods are empirical; consider correction factors (p. 49).
Energy ratio Er = Emeas / Etheor must be known; correct N accordingly (p. 50).
In sands correct for rod length and effective overburden (p. 50).
sections.applicability: SPT test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex F derived-value correlations for phi', settlement, and pile bearing resistance in sand.

sections.title: Use of test results and derived values
sections.summary: Heading for the use of SPT results and derived values: general criteria (4.6.4.1), bearing resistance (4.6.4.2) and settlement (4.6.4.3) of spread foundations in sand, and pile bearing resistance in sand (4.6.4.4).
sections.body: Heading for 4.6.4.1 to 4.6.4.4; it has no text of its own. (p. 50)
sections.applicability: SPT test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex F derived-value correlations for phi', settlement, and pile bearing resistance in sand.

sections.title: General criteria
sections.summary: In sands there is wide empirical SPT experience for density index, bearing resistance and settlement, but only as a rough approximation and mostly on uncorrected values; in clayey soil use is qualitative unless correlated locally with other tests.
sections.body: (1) In sands there is wide empirical experience, e.g. for density index, bearing resistance and settlement, though results are only a rough approximation and most methods still use uncorrected or partly corrected values. (2) There is no general agreement on SPT use in clayey soil; it should in principle be limited to a qualitative soil profile or a qualitative strength estimate. (3) It may sometimes be used quantitatively in clayey soil under well-known local conditions when directly correlated with other suitable tests. (p. 50)
key_points: SPT in sands: rough approximation; methods mostly use uncorrected values (p. 50).
In clayey soil, qualitative use only unless correlated locally (p. 50).
sections.applicability: SPT test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex F derived-value correlations for phi', settlement, and pile bearing resistance in sand.

sections.title: Bearing resistance of spread foundations in sands
sections.summary: For analytical bearing methods φ' may come from SPT directly or via density index (F.1, F.2; F.1 gives ID from N60 or (N1)60). Ageing raises blow counts and over-consolidation raises them for the same ID and σ'v0; both are allowed for, and φ' via F.2 can then be conservative.
sections.body: (1) For an analytical bearing method (examples in EN 1997-1:2004, Annex D), the effective angle of shearing resistance (φ') may be derived from SPT results. (2) φ' may be derived empirically from direct correlations with SPT results or from density index derived from SPT results; NOTE 1: see F.1 and F.2; NOTE 2: F.1 can give ID from N60 or (N1)60 (EN ISO 22476-3). (3) Sand's resistance to deformation often grows with the geological period of consolidation; this ageing raises blow counts and should be allowed for. (4) Over-consolidation raises blow counts for the same ID and σ'v0 and should be allowed for (p. 50). NOTE 1: F.1 shows correlations that allow for both ageing and over-consolidation. NOTE 2: after such corrections, φ' derived via density index from F.2 can be conservative (p. 51). (pp. 50 to 51)
key_points: φ' from SPT directly or via density index (F.1, F.2) (p. 50).
F.1 gives ID from N60 or (N1)60 (p. 50).
Ageing and over-consolidation raise blow counts; allow for them (p. 50).
φ' via F.2 after these corrections can be conservative (p. 51).
sections.applicability: SPT test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex F derived-value correlations for phi', settlement, and pile bearing resistance in sand.

sections.title: Settlement of spread foundations in sand
sections.summary: For elastic settlement methods E' may come from N-values or via density index from N60; direct methods compare N with plate tests or measured settlements, giving allowable bearing resistance for a maximum settlement of 25 mm or settlement at a given pressure; F.3 gives a sample method.
sections.body: (1) With a purely elastic method, the drained Young's modulus (E') may be derived from N-values by empirical correlations. (2) Alternatively the density index may be derived from N60 and E' found from it by a suitable correlation. (3) Direct design methods rest on comparing N-values with plate loading tests or measured foundation settlements; allowable bearing resistance for a maximum settlement of 25 mm, or the settlement for a given pressure, follows from them with reference to footing width, embedment and groundwater table position. NOTE: the sample method in F.3 can be used. (p. 51)
key_points: E' from N-values or via density index from N60 (p. 51).
Direct methods give allowable bearing resistance for a maximum settlement of 25 mm (p. 51).
F.3 gives a sample settlement method for sand (p. 51).
sections.applicability: SPT test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex F derived-value correlations for phi', settlement, and pile bearing resistance in sand.

sections.title: Pile bearing resistance in sand
sections.summary: Ultimate compressive or tensile pile resistance from SPT (EN 1997-1:2004, 7.6.2.3 or 7.6.3.3) uses rules from locally established correlations between static load tests and SPT results.
sections.body: (1)P If ultimate compressive or tensile pile resistance is derived from SPT results per EN 1997-1:2004, 7.6.2.3 or 7.6.3.3, calculation rules based on locally established correlations between static load test and SPT results shall be used. (p. 51)
key_points: Pile resistance from SPT needs locally established load test correlations (p. 51).
sections.applicability: SPT test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex F derived-value correlations for phi', settlement, and pile bearing resistance in sand.

sections.title: Dynamic probing tests (DP)
sections.summary: Heading for dynamic probing tests (DP): objectives (4.7.1), requirements (4.7.2), evaluation (4.7.3) and use of results (4.7.4).
sections.body: Heading for 4.7.1 to 4.7.4; it has no text of its own. (p. 51)
sections.applicability: DP (DPL/DPM/DPH/DPSH) test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex G derived-value correlations for phi', oedometer modulus, and qc estimation.

sections.title: Objectives
sections.summary: DP measures in-situ resistance of soil and soft rock to dynamic cone penetration: blows of a given hammer and fall per set penetration, recorded continuously with depth, no samples. Used for soil profiles with sampling, relative comparison, strength and deformation by correlation, and depth to very dense layers.
sections.body: (1) Dynamic probing determines the in-situ resistance of soil and soft rock to dynamic penetration of a cone. (2)P A hammer of given mass and fall drives the cone; penetration resistance is the number of blows to drive the penetrometer a set distance; a continuous record with depth shall be provided; no samples are taken. (3) Results should be used especially for soil profiles with Section 3 sampling, or as a relative comparison with other in-situ tests. (4) They may also give strength and deformation properties, generally of coarse soil and possibly fine soil, through suitable correlations. (5) They can show the depth to very dense layers, e.g. for end bearing pile length. (p. 51)
key_points: DP: blows to drive a cone a set distance, continuous record, no samples (p. 51).
Mainly for soil profiles with sampling (p. 51).
Shows depth to very dense layers, e.g. end bearing pile length (p. 51).
sections.applicability: DP (DPL/DPM/DPH/DPSH) test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex G derived-value correlations for phi', oedometer modulus, and qc estimation.

sections.title: Specific requirements
sections.summary: The DP type per EN ISO 22476-2 is decided; five procedures: DPL (N10L), DPM (N10M), DPH (N10H), DPSH-A and DPSH-B (N10SA or N20SA, N10SB or N20SB). Deviations, e.g. a 10 cm2 DPM cone instead of 15 cm2, are justified; lighter kit may serve where access is hard.
sections.body: (1)P Beyond 4.2.1, the type of DP test per EN ISO 22476-2 shall be decided. (2)P Tests shall be performed and reported per EN ISO 22476-2. NOTE: five procedures cover a wide range of specific work per blow: dynamic probing light (DPL), the lower end of the mass range, blow count N10L; medium (DPM), the medium mass range, N10M; heavy (DPH), the medium to very heavy range, N10H; super heavy (DPSH-A and DPSH-B), the upper end, closely related to SPT dimensions, N10SA or N20SA, N10SB or N20SB. (3)P Deviations from EN ISO 22476-2 shall be justified with comment on their influence; NOTE: deviations exist in fall height and hammer mass and in cone dimensions, e.g. a 10 cm2 DPM cone instead of the 15 cm2 of EN ISO 22476-2:2005, clause 4. (4) Where access is especially difficult, lighter equipment and other procedures may be used. (p. 52)
key_points: Decide the DP type per EN ISO 22476-2 (p. 52).
DPL N10L, DPM N10M, DPH N10H, DPSH-A/B N10SA, N20SA, N10SB, N20SB (p. 52).
Known deviation: 10 cm2 DPM cone instead of 15 cm2 (p. 52).
sections.applicability: DP (DPL/DPM/DPH/DPSH) test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex G derived-value correlations for phi', oedometer modulus, and qc estimation.

sections.title: Evaluation of test results
sections.summary: Evaluation uses the EN ISO 22476-2 field and test reports and considers ground and equipment influences on penetration resistance per EN ISO 22476-2:2005, 5.4.
sections.body: (1)P Beyond 4.2, the EN ISO 22476-2 field and test reports shall be used. (2)P Ground and equipment influences on penetration resistance per EN ISO 22476-2:2005, 5.4 shall be considered. (p. 52)
key_points: Consider influences per EN ISO 22476-2:2005, 5.4 (p. 52).
sections.applicability: DP (DPL/DPM/DPH/DPSH) test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex G derived-value correlations for phi', oedometer modulus, and qc estimation.

sections.title: Use of test results and derived values
sections.summary: In coarse soil DP correlations serve design if rod friction is negligible or corrected; in fine soil only under known local conditions, minding skin friction. Published correlations lack measured energy (Annex G, conservative): φ' via ID (G.1, G.2), Eoed (G.3), qc from N10 or N20 (G.4), DP-to-DP (G.5).
sections.body: (1) In coarse soil, correlations with some parameters and field tests can be used quantitatively for foundation design if rod friction is negligible or duly corrected. (2) In fine soil, quantitative use should be only under well-known local conditions with specific correlations; skin friction is of special concern and should be allowed for. (3) Correlations between DP tests and with other tests or parameters often eliminate or correct rod friction but have not measured the energy transmitted, so they are not generally valid; NOTE 1: examples are in Annex G (p. 52); NOTE 2: Annex G correlations should be taken as conservative. (4) For an analytical bearing method (example in EN 1997-1:2004, D.4), φ' of coarse soil may come from blow counts and the corresponding density index (ID) by correlation (examples in G.1 and G.2). (5) For theoretical elastic settlement methods (EN 1997-1:2004, Annex F), Eoed from blow counts may be used (examples in G.3). (6) Where established correlations between static pile load tests (EN 1997-1:2004, 7.6.2.3) and qc in coarse soil are used, qc may be estimated from N10 or N20 by established relationships; NOTE 1: DPH examples in G.4; NOTE 2: G.5 correlates different DP tests (p. 53). (pp. 52 to 53)
key_points: Coarse soil: quantitative use if rod friction negligible or corrected (p. 52).
Fine soil: only under well-known local conditions; mind skin friction (p. 52).
Annex G correlations are conservative estimates (p. 53).
φ' via ID (G.1, G.2); Eoed (G.3); qc from N10 or N20 (G.4) (p. 53).
sections.applicability: DP (DPL/DPM/DPH/DPSH) test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex G derived-value correlations for phi', oedometer modulus, and qc estimation.

sections.title: Weight sounding test (WST)
sections.summary: Heading for the weight sounding test (WST): objectives (4.8.1), requirements (4.8.2), evaluation (4.8.3) and use of results (4.8.4).
sections.body: Heading for 4.8.1 to 4.8.4; it has no text of its own. (p. 53)
sections.applicability: WST test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex H derived-value correlation, plus general guidance on WST use in coarse and fine soil.

sections.title: Objectives
sections.summary: The WST measures in-situ resistance to static and/or rotational penetration of a screw-shaped point: static in soft soil below 1 kN, otherwise rotated with half-turns counted; continuous record, no samples. Used for soil profiles and layer sequence, density index of coarse soil and depth to very dense layers.
sections.body: (1) The WST determines the in-situ resistance of soil to static and/or rotational penetration of a screw-shaped point. (2)P It shall be a static sounding in soft soil where resistance is below 1 kN; above 1 kN the penetrometer shall be rotated, manually or mechanically, and the half-turns for a given penetration recorded; a continuous record with depth is provided but no samples. NOTE: see CEN ISO/TS 22476-10 (X.3.5). (3) The WST should mainly give a continuous soil profile and the layer sequence; it penetrates well even in stiff clays and dense sands. (4) It may estimate the density index of coarse soil. (5) It can show the depth to very dense layers, e.g. for end bearing pile length. (p. 53)
key_points: Static sounding below 1 kN; rotated with half-turns counted above 1 kN (p. 53).
Mainly for continuous soil profile and layer sequence (p. 53).
Can estimate density index of coarse soil (p. 53).
sections.applicability: WST test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex H derived-value correlation, plus general guidance on WST use in coarse and fine soil.

sections.title: Specific requirements
sections.summary: WSTs are performed and reported by a recognised method (CEN ISO/TS 22476-10 gives one); deviations are justified with their influence on results commented on.
sections.body: (1) Tests should be performed and reported by a recognised method (p. 53). (2)P Deviations from that method shall be justified with comment on their influence. NOTE: see CEN ISO/TS 22476-10 (p. 54). (pp. 53 to 54)
key_points: WST by a recognised method; see CEN ISO/TS 22476-10 (p. 54).
sections.applicability: WST test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex H derived-value correlation, plus general guidance on WST use in coarse and fine soil.

sections.title: Evaluation of test results
sections.summary: Evaluation follows 4.2 and the method's reports. Influences: layer sequence; very soft to firm clays below 1 kN or under 10 half-turns per 0,2 m, strength needing site calibration for sensitivity; medium dense to dense silts and fine sands 10 to 30 half-turns per 0,2 m; coarse gravel resistance may mislead.
sections.body: (1)P Evaluation shall follow 4.2. (2) The field and test reports of the 4.8.2 (1) method should be used (NOTE: CEN ISO/TS 22476-10). (3) Influences on evaluation: resistance with depth can follow the layer sequence; in very soft to firm clays resistance is often below 1 kN or about constant and below 10 half-turns per 0,2 m; clay sensitivity affects resistance, so strength needs a calibration for each site; very loose to loose silt and sand give rather low, constant resistance; medium dense to dense silts and fine sands give higher resistance (10 to 30 half-turns per 0,2 m), about constant with depth; in sand and gravel the scatter grows with grain size; in silty sands and coarse gravel high resistance does not always mean higher density, strength or stiffness. (p. 54)
key_points: Very soft to firm clays: below 1 kN or under 10 half-turns per 0,2 m (p. 54).
Clay strength from WST needs a calibration for each site (p. 54).
Medium dense to dense silts and fine sands: 10 to 30 half-turns per 0,2 m (p. 54).
High resistance in silty sands and coarse gravel may mislead (p. 54).
sections.applicability: WST test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex H derived-value correlation, plus general guidance on WST use in coarse and fine soil.

sections.title: Use of test results and derived values
sections.summary: Spread foundation design from WST is analytical: φ' from correlations based on comparable experience (Annex H, quartz and feldspar sands of a European region); E' for adjusted elasticity settlement on local experience; direct bearing estimates in coarse soil; cu in fine soil on local experience.
sections.body: (1)P Bearing resistance or settlement of a spread foundation from WST results shall use an analytical method. (2) For an analytical bearing method (examples in EN 1997-1:2004, Annex D), φ' may come from correlations with weight sounding resistance. (3) Such correlations should rest on comparable experience relevant to the design situation; NOTE: Annex H gives an example for quartz and feldspar sands in a European region. (4) For an adjusted elasticity settlement method, the drained Young's modulus (E') may come from weight sounding resistance on local experience (p. 54); for quartz and feldspar sands, e.g., φ' may be estimated from it. NOTE 1: such a method is in EN 1997-1:2004, Annex F. NOTE 2: Annex H gives example correlations for E' and φ' of quartz and feldspar sands. (5) In coarse soil the resistance may also give direct bearing capacity estimates for spread foundations and piles. (6) In fine soil it may estimate undrained shear strength on local experience, considering sensitivity and borehole water conditions (p. 55). (pp. 54 to 55)
key_points: Spread foundation design from WST uses an analytical method (p. 54).
φ' and E' correlations need comparable or local experience; Annex H example (p. 54).
Coarse soil: direct bearing estimates for spread foundations and piles (p. 55).
Fine soil: cu on local experience, considering sensitivity (p. 55).
sections.applicability: WST test procedure, evaluation, and the Annex H derived-value correlation, plus general guidance on WST use in coarse and fine soil.

sections.title: Field vane test (FVT)
sections.summary: Heading for the field vane test (FVT): objectives (4.9.1), requirements (4.9.2), evaluation (4.9.3) and use of results (4.9.4).
sections.body: Heading for 4.9.1 to 4.9.4; it has no text of its own. (p. 55)
sections.applicability: FVT test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex I correction-factor methods for deriving cu from raw vane strength.

sections.title: Objectives
sections.summary: The FVT measures in-situ resistance to rotation of a vane in soft fine soil for undrained shear strength and sensitivity, using a rectangular vane of four plates at 90° pushed in and rotated; it may also serve in stiff clays, silts and glacial clays; remoulded strength after extensive rotation gives sensitivity.
sections.body: (1) The FVT measures in situ the resistance to rotation of a vane in soft fine soil to determine undrained shear strength and sensitivity. (2)P It shall use a rectangular vane of four plates fixed at 90° to each other, pushed to the desired depth and rotated. (3) It may also give undrained shear strength in stiff clays, silts and glacial clays, with reliability varying by soil type. (4) After extensive rotation thoroughly remoulds the soil along the failure surface, the remoulded shear strength can be measured and the sensitivity calculated. (p. 55)
key_points: Rectangular vane of four plates at 90°, pushed in and rotated (p. 55).
Gives undrained shear strength and sensitivity in soft fine soil (p. 55).
Remoulded strength after extensive rotation gives sensitivity (p. 55).
sections.applicability: FVT test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex I correction-factor methods for deriving cu from raw vane strength.

sections.title: Specific requirements
sections.summary: FVTs should be performed and reported per EN ISO 22476-9; deviations are justified with their influence commented on.
sections.body: (1) Tests should be performed and reported per EN ISO 22476-9. (2)P Deviations shall be justified with comment on their influence on results. (p. 55)
key_points: FVT per EN ISO 22476-9 (p. 55).
sections.applicability: FVT test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex I correction-factor methods for deriving cu from raw vane strength.

sections.title: Evaluation of test results
sections.summary: Evaluation uses the EN ISO 22476-9 field and test reports; results of other field tests (CPT, SPT, WST or DP) should be available and considered.
sections.body: (1)P Beyond 4.2, the EN ISO 22476-9 field and test reports shall be used. (2) Results of other field tests, e.g. CPT, SPT, WST or DP if done, should be available and considered. (p. 55)
key_points: Consider other field tests (CPT, SPT, WST, DP) with the FVT (p. 55).
sections.applicability: FVT test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex I correction-factor methods for deriving cu from raw vane strength.

sections.title: Use of test results and derived values
sections.summary: Bearing, pile and slope design from vane results is analytical; the test result cfv is corrected to cu = μ × cfv (Eq. 4.4), μ from local experience; existing factors relate to liquid limit, plasticity index, effective vertical stress or degree of consolidation (Annex I).
sections.body: (1)P Spread foundation bearing resistance, ultimate compressive or tensile pile resistance or slope stability derived from vane results shall use an analytical method. (2)P To derive undrained shear strength, the test result (cfv) shall be corrected by Eq. 4.4, with μ determined on local experience. (3) Existing correction factors usually relate to the liquid limit, plasticity index, effective vertical stress or degree of consolidation. NOTE: Annex I gives examples (p. 56). (pp. 55 to 56)
key_points: Use an analytical method for design from vane results (p. 56).
cu = μ × cfv (Eq. 4.4); μ from local experience (p. 56).
Annex I gives example correction factors (p. 56).

equations.description: cu = μ × cfv; derived undrained shear strength from the field vane test result cfv, μ correction factor determined on local experience (p. 56)

sections.applicability: FVT test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex I correction-factor methods for deriving cu from raw vane strength.

sections.title: Flat dilatometer test (DMT)
sections.summary: Heading for the flat dilatometer test (DMT): objectives (4.10.1), requirements (4.10.2), evaluation (4.10.3) and use of results (4.10.4).
sections.body: Heading for 4.10.1 to 4.10.4; it has no text of its own. (p. 56)
sections.applicability: DMT test procedure, evaluation, and the derived-value equations for undrained shear strength (Eq 4.5) and oedometer modulus (Annex J).

sections.title: Objectives
sections.summary: The DMT expands a thin circular steel membrane flush on a blade pushed vertically into the ground, reading pressures at lift-off and at 1,10 mm centre displacement, at chosen depths or semi-continuously; it gives stratigraphy, in-situ stress, deformation and shear strength, mainly in clays, silts and sands.
sections.body: (1) The DMT determines in-situ strength and deformation properties of soil by expanding a thin circular steel membrane mounted flush on one face of a blade-shaped probe inserted vertically. (2)P Pressures are measured when the membrane, flush with the blade, just starts to move and when its centre has displaced 1,10 mm into the soil; tests shall be at selected depths or semi-continuous. (3) Results may give stratigraphy, in-situ stress state, deformation properties and shear strength. (4) The DMT should mainly be used in clays, silts and sands with particles small compared with the membrane. NOTE: see CEN ISO/TS 22476-11 (X.3.7). (p. 56)
key_points: Pressures at membrane lift-off and at 1,10 mm centre displacement (p. 56).
Gives stratigraphy, in-situ stress, deformation and shear strength (p. 56).
Mainly in clays, silts and sands with small particles (p. 56).
sections.applicability: DMT test procedure, evaluation, and the derived-value equations for undrained shear strength (Eq 4.5) and oedometer modulus (Annex J).

sections.title: Specific requirements
sections.summary: DMTs should follow a recognised method (CEN ISO/TS 22476-11 gives one); deviations are justified with their influence commented on.
sections.body: (1) Tests should be performed and reported by a recognised method. (2)P Deviations from it shall be justified with comment on their influence. NOTE: see CEN ISO/TS 22476-11. (p. 56)
key_points: DMT by a recognised method; see CEN ISO/TS 22476-11 (p. 56).
sections.applicability: DMT test procedure, evaluation, and the derived-value equations for undrained shear strength (Eq 4.5) and oedometer modulus (Annex J).

sections.title: Evaluation of test results
sections.summary: DMT evaluation follows 4.2 and uses the field and test reports of the 4.10.2 (1) method (CEN ISO/TS 22476-11).
sections.body: (1)P Evaluation shall follow 4.2 (p. 56). (2) The field and test reports of the 4.10.2 (1) method should also be used. NOTE: see CEN ISO/TS 22476-11 (p. 57). (pp. 56 to 57)
key_points: Use the 4.10.2 (1) method's reports; see CEN ISO/TS 22476-11 (p. 57).
sections.applicability: DMT test procedure, evaluation, and the derived-value equations for undrained shear strength (Eq 4.5) and oedometer modulus (Annex J).

sections.title: Use of test results and derived values
sections.summary: Heading for the use of DMT results and derived values: spread foundation bearing resistance and settlement (4.10.4.1) and pile bearing resistance (4.10.4.2).
sections.body: Heading for 4.10.4.1 and 4.10.4.2; it has no text of its own. (p. 57)
sections.applicability: DMT test procedure, evaluation, and the derived-value equations for undrained shear strength (Eq 4.5) and oedometer modulus (Annex J).

sections.title: Bearing resistance and settlement of spread foundations
sections.summary: Spread foundation bearing resistance from DMT is analytical; cu of non-cemented clays with IDMT < 0,8 from cu = 0,22 σ'v0 × (0,5 KDMT)^1,25 (Eq. 4.5). One-dimensional settlement may use a DMT tangent modulus Eoed; in fine soil only while σ'v0 plus the load increase stays below pre-consolidation (Annex J).
sections.body: (1)P Spread foundation bearing resistance from DMT results shall use an analytical method. (2) With an analytical method (examples in EN 1997-1:2004, Annex D), cu of non-cemented clays whose DMT material index IDMT < 0,8 may be found from Eq. 4.5, KDMT being the horizontal stress index, or from any other well-documented relationship based on local experience. (3) With an adjusted elasticity method (EN 1997-1:2004, Annex F), one-dimensional settlement may use the one-dimensional tangent modulus (Eoed) from DMT; in fine soil only when effective overburden plus the foundation-induced stress increase is below the pre-consolidation pressure (example in Annex J). (p. 57)
key_points: Bearing resistance from DMT uses an analytical method (p. 57).
Eq. 4.5 for cu of non-cemented clays with IDMT < 0,8 (p. 57).
DMT Eoed in fine soil only below the pre-consolidation pressure (p. 57).

equations.description: cu = 0,22 σ'v0 × (0,5 KDMT)^1,25; undrained shear strength of non-cemented clays with material index IDMT < 0,8, σ'v0 effective vertical overburden stress, KDMT horizontal stress index (p. 57)

sections.summary: Ultimate compressive or tensile pile resistance from DMT results uses an analytical method for base and shaft resistance.
sections.body: (1)P If ultimate compressive or tensile pile resistance is derived from DMT results, an analytical method shall derive base and shaft resistance. (p. 57)

sections.title: Plate loading test (PLT)
sections.summary: Heading for the plate loading test (PLT): objectives (4.11.1), requirements (4.11.2), evaluation (4.11.3) and use of results (4.11.4).
sections.body: Heading for 4.11.1 to 4.11.4; it has no text of its own. (p. 57)

sections.title: Objectives
sections.summary: The PLT records load and settlement of a rigid plate modelling a foundation to give vertical deformation and strength of soil and rock masses in situ, on a levelled undisturbed surface at ground level, an excavation bottom, a large borehole, shaft or gallery; not normally in very soft fine soil.
sections.body: (1) The PLT determines in-situ vertical deformation and strength of soil and rock masses by recording load and settlement as a rigid plate modelling a foundation loads the ground. (2)P It shall be done on a thoroughly levelled, undisturbed surface at ground level, at an excavation bottom at some depth, or at the bottom of a large-diameter borehole, exploration shaft or gallery (p. 57). (3) It applies to all soils, fills and rock but normally should not be used in very soft fine soil (p. 58). (pp. 57 to 58)
key_points: Rigid plate load-settlement record on a levelled, undisturbed surface (p. 57).
Not normally in very soft fine soil (p. 58).
sections.applicability: PLT test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex K derived-value equations for cu, modulus, sub-grade reaction, and sand settlement.

sections.title: Specific requirements
sections.summary: PLTs follow EN ISO 22476-13; deviations, e.g. in plate size or procedure (incremental loading, constant rate of deformation), are justified with their influence commented on.
sections.body: (1)P Tests shall be performed and reported per EN ISO 22476-13. (2)P Deviations shall be justified with comment on their influence. NOTE: deviations exist, e.g. in plate size and procedure (incremental loading, constant rate of deformation). (p. 58)
key_points: PLT per EN ISO 22476-13 (p. 58).
sections.applicability: PLT test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex K derived-value equations for cu, modulus, sub-grade reaction, and sand settlement.

sections.title: Evaluation of test results
sections.summary: Evaluation uses, beyond 4.2, the EN ISO 22476-13 field and test reports.
sections.body: (1)P Beyond 4.2, the EN ISO 22476-13 field and test reports shall be used. (p. 58)
key_points: Use the EN ISO 22476-13 reports (p. 58).
sections.applicability: PLT test procedure, evaluation, and the full set of Annex K derived-value equations for cu, modulus, sub-grade reaction, and sand settlement.

sections.title: Use of test results and derived values
sections.summary: PLT results predict spread foundation behaviour: parameters need a homogeneous layer of at least twice the plate width; direct design needs a plate sized to the foundation or a homogeneous layer to twice its width. Fast constant-rate tests give cu (K.1); EPLT gives E (K.2); incremental tests give ks (K.3); sand footings (K.4).
sections.body: (1) PLT results may predict spread foundation behaviour. (2) For parameters of a homogeneous layer (indirect design), the layer beneath the plate should be at least two times the plate width or diameter thick. (3) Results may serve direct design only if the plate size was chosen for the planned foundation width (observations transformed directly) or a homogeneous layer exists to two times the planned foundation width (smaller plate results transformed empirically to the foundation size). (4) For analytical bearing methods (EN 1997-1:2004, Annex D), cu may come from a PLT at constant rate of penetration fast enough to practically preclude drainage (example in K.1). (5) For an adjusted elasticity settlement method (EN 1997-1:2004, Annex F), Young's modulus (E) may come from the plate settlement modulus (EPLT) on established experience (EPLT in K.2). (6) The coefficient of subgrade reaction (ks) may come from an incremental loading test (example in K.3) (p. 58). (7) For direct design, PLT results may be transferred directly to the foundation without parameters. (8) Settlements of footings in sand may be derived from PLT results (example in K.4) (p. 59). (pp. 58 to 59)
key_points: Homogeneous layer at least two times the plate width for parameters (p. 58).
Direct design needs plate sized to the footing or homogeneous layer to twice its width (p. 58).
cu from fast constant-rate tests (K.1); E from EPLT (K.2) (p. 58).
ks from incremental loading (K.3); sand footing settlement (K.4) (pp. 58 to 59).
